nodes.label: Billing group (subscription keyed by id, not org)
nodes.rationale: Second orgs exist for a payout reason (one org = one Connect account = one bank account), and charging a second full software subscription for what is really a bank-account boundary reads as a rip-off. Stripe forces per-org Connect; it does not force per-org subscriptions, so that part is a commercial choice this changes. No new table — subscriptions gains its own identity and orgs point at it.

nodes.label: quantity_paid
nodes.rationale: A local record of what has been PAID FOR this period so a removed org's slot stays reusable at no charge until renewal. It is NOT what Stripe bills from — Stripe cuts renewals from the item quantity. Written only after Stripe confirms, so the reconcile sweep's quantity_paid <> active_org_count predicate stays honest.

nodes.label: Stripe graduated tiered price (base + half-price extras)
nodes.rationale: No org is ever flagged as 'the extra one' — quantity is a count. Pinning a $19 price to org A and $9 to org B would strand B on the extra-org rate for ever if A were deleted. Extra orgs are half the plan's base price rather than a flat $9 because after V309 an org slot buys a FEE RATE, and a flat rate would let a reseller sell 1% slots for 2.5x less than the tier.

nodes.label: syncGroupQuantity / the only sync rule
nodes.rationale: Increment prorates and charges immediately; decrement must still reach Stripe with proration_behavior:'none' — the original 'renewal trues it up' wording was wrong and shipped, because Stripe never recomputes from our database at cycle time. Suspended orgs still count: suspension is moderation, not billing. Only deleted_at removes an org from the bill.

nodes.label: invalidateGroupEntitlements (cache fan-out)
nodes.rationale: Keys are ent:<orgId>:* and invalidateOrgEntitlements drops exactly one org, so after grouping a plan change on the group leaves every other org serving stale entitlements for the 300s TTL. Named the highest-risk edit in the change.

nodes.label: Attach an org to a billing group
nodes.rationale: Owner-gated on both orgs — admin is an operational role, not a financial one. Refuses past_due and cancel_at_period_end because an attach must never mutate subscription state as a side effect. A failed increment invoice does not roll the attach back: it enters normal dunning, so there is one failure mode, not two.

nodes.label: Detach an org from a billing group
nodes.rationale: Either side may initiate: nobody needs permission from the person funding them in order to leave, and no payer is trapped. Requires no payment; comped_until carries the org through the already-paid period with no scheduler and no new column, and inheriting trial_used_at stops detach farming a fresh 14 days. Blocking prerequisite: webhooks resolving via metadata.org_id become actively wrong once detach ships, so subscription_id must be stamped into Stripe metadata in the same change.

nodes.label: Transfer a billing group
nodes.rationale: Distinct from transfer-owner, which moves org ownership and never touches billing. Without it a group changing hands means detaching every org and re-grouping, losing the group and re-charging tier 1. The card is not moved — the new owner re-enters it.

nodes.label: L1 — staff suspend would kill a whole group's billing
nodes.rationale: Suspension writes organizations.status only and never touches the subscription; a suspended org keeps counting toward quantity because suspension is moderation and dropping the slot would hand a discount for being moderated.

nodes.label: L2 — billing gates on the group owner, Connect on the org owner
nodes.rationale: requireBillingOwner gates on the active org's owner role, so after a transfer-owner the new org owner would get the group's card, invoices and cancel button. Connect stays gated on the org's owner because it is the club's bank account; billing gates on subscriptions.owner_user_id.

nodes.label: L3 — one tax ID cannot cover two legal entities
nodes.rationale: Tax ID, billing address and promo codes all hang off the Stripe customer, so a group has one of each. Two clubs that are two registered charities cannot legally share an invoice — this is the real, non-cosmetic reason detach exists, and detach copy should say so.

nodes.label: org_has_feature SQL resolver
nodes.rationale: The resolver exists twice (TS resolveFromDb and the security-definer SQL function) and both must change together; entitlements-sql-parity.test.ts is the tie that fails loudly if only one is updated. The SQL resolver feeds the public site, so grouping reaches public pages, not just the console.

nodes.label: orgs.max_owned cap as a group property
nodes.rationale: Community stays at exactly one org because quotas resolve per org — a second free org multiplies the free grant and one active competition is the free tier's entire lever. V309 weakens the argument (a community org now pays 8% on entries), but quota multiplication is real regardless of revenue and the cap is reversible in one plan_entitlements row.

nodes.label: Grouping re-rates registration.fee_percent
nodes.rationale: fee_percent resolves from the group's plan, so attaching an org moves its entry-fee cut immediately (8% → 2% → 1%). The strongest argument for the feature and the line the attach UI should lead with; it also makes the federation decision arithmetic (break-even around $21,000 of annual entries across the group).

nodes.label: Rejected: a stripe_quantity mirror column
nodes.rationale: A third number that can go stale independently is the failure mode being removed, not one to add. Ordering the quantity_paid write after Stripe's confirmation buys the same property with nothing new to keep in step. Accepted blind spot: an out-of-band Stripe dashboard edit is invisible to either scheme.
